# KafScale

> Kafka-compatible streaming platform. Scale streaming and analytics cloud-native on S3. Automated.

KafScale is an open source streaming platform. Brokers are stateless, S3 is the source of truth, and the license is Apache 2.0. It gives you up to 90% lower storage cost than Kafka on replicated broker disks. Metadata lives in etcd inside your own Kubernetes cluster, and data is stored in the open, documented .kfs segment format.

Full text for LLMs: https://kafscale.io/llms-full.txt

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://kafscale.io/docs/): Guides and reference for running KafScale
- [Quickstart](https://kafscale.io/quickstart/): Install the operator, create a topic, and stream messages
- [User guide](https://kafscale.io/user-guide/): How to use KafScale after it is deployed
- [Architecture](https://kafscale.io/architecture/): How brokers, S3, etcd, and the operator fit together
- [Rationale](https://kafscale.io/rationale/): Why KafScale uses stateless brokers and object storage
- [Supported storage](https://kafscale.io/supported/): S3-compatible backends and what each one requires
- [Operations](https://kafscale.io/operations/): Production install, hardening, and day-to-day operations
- [Security](https://kafscale.io/security/): Current security posture and how to report a vulnerability
- [mTLS authentication](https://kafscale.io/kafka-authentication/): TLS 1.3 and mTLS for Kafka clients at the KafScale proxy. URI SAN to principal mapping, broker ACLs, Secrets, Helm and CRD fields, certificate rotation
- [Protocol compatibility](https://kafscale.io/protocol/): Kafka APIs the broker advertises
- [Latency and batching](https://kafscale.io/latency/): KafScale latency is S3 latency. How produce and fetch map to S3 requests, AWS published S3 latency figures with sources, producer batching settings, and the deliberate trade-offs (no compaction, transactions or idempotent producers)
- [Comparison](https://kafscale.io/comparison/): How KafScale compares with other Kafka-compatible platforms
- [Migrate from WarpStream](https://kafscale.io/migrate-from-warpstream/): Move topics from WarpStream with a kaf-mirror dual run and cutover, and what KafScale does not support
- [Bento with KafScale](https://kafscale.io/bento/): Run Bento pipelines against KafScale with the kafka_franz input and output
- [Project overview](https://kafscale.io/overview/): What KafScale optimizes for, and what it leaves out
- [Release notes](https://kafscale.io/releases/): Changes, upgrade notes and fixes for each release

## Related projects

- [KafClaw](https://github.com/KafClaw/KafClaw): Agent runtime in Go that connects AI agents through Kafka topics. Its workshop setup runs on a KafScale broker and the KafScale LFS proxy
- [KafGraph](https://github.com/scalytics/KafGraph): Shared knowledge graph for agents. Runs as a KafScale processor and reads KafClaw group topics
- [kafSIEM](https://github.com/scalytics/kafSIEM): Entity graph over Kafka agent traffic and OSINT feeds. Can consume from KafScale
- [kaf-mirror](https://github.com/scalytics/kaf-mirror): Kafka-to-Kafka replication, used for the WarpStream migration guide
- [kshark-core](https://github.com/scalytics/kshark-core): Kafka connectivity diagnostics. An example of how agents can use our tools to debug Kafka clusters
- [infinimesh](https://infinimesh.org/): Self-hosted IoT device platform. Its Kafka addon streams device data to KafScale
- [Scalytics open source](https://www.scalytics.io/open-source): All Scalytics open source projects
- [Lascaris](https://www.scalytics.io/lascaris): Governed AI agents on Kafka, the supported Scalytics product built on this open core

## Author

- [Alexander Alten](https://www.novatechflow.com/p/kafscale.html): Created KafScale. CTO at Scalytics. Writes at novatechflow.com
